engineering-preview-terminated-on-every-exitengineering-verification-tooling-robustness0.625 of 0.625 (major)passAll four scripts (verify and inspect, repository and bootstrap copies) share one startPreview. It spawns `node node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js preview` directly through process.execPath, so the child is the Vite preview server itself, not an npm or npx wrapper. stopPreview sends SIGTERM to that child, awaits its &#39;exit&#39; event (capped at 3s), then sends SIGKILL if it is still alive. Every script starts the preview and the browser inside a try whose finally runs `await browser?.close(); await stopPreview(preview?.child)`. Success, a failing check, a chromium() launch failure and any later error therefore all close the server. Repository verify returns early on build or sample failure before any preview starts. installSignalCleanup covers SIGINT and SIGTERM. Judge C fails this on two points, and neither decides the requirement. (1) The readiness-timeout branch in startPreview sends SIGTERM without awaiting. That path runs before the preview has started, so it is not one of the named post-start exit paths. It still signals the Vite server itself, not a wrapper. (2) The un-awaited SIGKILL escalation fires only if the server ignores SIGTERM for 3s. In that case the awaited cleanup has already been attempted and the forced kill goes to the server process itself. The requirement asks that the server, not a wrapper, be terminated and awaited on success, on browser launch failure and on post-start errors. Lines 50-55 and the finally blocks do exactly that. testing-evidence-traceable-coveragetesting-evidence-quality-criteria0 of 1 (major)failThe requirement is not met. The candidate chose to leave a substantial share of the specified user-visible behavior unexercised, and none of those omissions is environmental. 1) Requirement-003 has 14 scenarios (packet.txt:174-211). Seven were never exercised: &#39;Missing sample fails&#39;, &#39;Console or page error fails verification&#39;, &#39;Step error fails verification&#39;, &#39;Suspicious overlap is reported&#39;, &#39;Intentional overlap can be marked&#39;, &#39;Indistinct active chrome is reported&#39; and &#39;Unpolished attribution is reported&#39;. &#39;Clear outcome&#39; was never observed through `npm run verify` either. The only observations recorded are a passing build and the inspection helper reporting no warnings on the clean sample (packet.txt:1215-1216, 1266). The helper was runnable in this environment. The test plan&#39;s own definitions of these behaviors (INT-002 warnings and exemptions at packet.txt:1512-1518; E2E-002 failure phases at packet.txt:1530-1536) show they are product command behaviors, not separate-agent skill journeys. The log says why it skipped them: the &#39;process-failure ... runs were not added&#39; because they are &#39;owned by E2E-002/INT-001 and the automated-suite boundary excludes rerunning them&#39; (packet.txt:1220), and fault injection is out of scope (packet.txt:1236, 1276-1277). That is a scope choice, not an environmental impediment. 2) The motion scenarios &#39;Persisting entity morphs&#39;, &#39;New entity enters after others settle&#39; and &#39;Continuing entities are not faded as newcomers&#39; (packet.txt:44-58) were checked only against a weaker property. The record shows only that DOM nodes stayed mounted and new nodes appeared (packet.txt:1208). It does not show morphing, newcomers waiting until continuing motion settles, or the absence of fades. The criterion says that kind of weaker check does not cover a scenario. AT-003 also names these motion outcomes explicitly (packet.txt:1568). Judges A and B treated these omissions as environmental or as a minority. The cited log lines attribute the verifier and warning omissions to the acceptance-suite boundary (packet.txt:1215, 1220, 1236), not to an unavailable agent. The criterion excuses only environmental impediments; a disclosed scope choice still counts against coverage. Together, half of requirement-003 plus the continuity motion scenarios is a substantial share of the specified behavior. Judge B also acknowledged that DOM persistence is weaker than motion sequencing. The NaN reaches `browser.newPage({ viewport })` or `page.waitForTimeout`, which throw an unhelpful Playwright error. A flag's value can also be picked up as the slug: line 8 takes the first argument that doesn't start with `--`, so `npm run inspect -- --width 390 my-slug` uses `390` as the slug and navigates to the wrong route.\n ✓ Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - scripts/preview-utils.mjs:28 The readiness probe can report success for the wrong server. When a user-supplied `--port` is already held by another HTTP server, the vite child started with `--strictPort` exits, but the loop checks `child.exitCode` before the fetch. If the other server answers 200 first, `startPreview` returns ready. The delete-before-copy order also means any mid-copy error leaves the snapshot destroyed.\n ✓ Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/preview-utils.mjs:28 Precondition: `FORCE_COLOR` is set, or Vite otherwise emits ANSI codes on piped stdio. Trace: readiness is gated on the regex `/Local:\\s+https?:\\/\\//` over captured output. Vite colours the URL, so an escape sequence sits between the whitespace and `http`. The regex never matches, the loop keeps calling `delay(50)` and `continue`, and the fetch probe is never reached. Failure: after 15s `startPreview` throws 'preview readiness timed out', even though the server is up. `npm run verify` and `npm run inspect` fail, and the preview child is killed.\n ✓ Fixed: review_skills_skill-quality (1) - skills/presentation/SKILL.md:3 Description is third-person but trigger phrases are generic (\"make a presentation\", \"slide-like visual story\"). The skill does not say what it will not do, such as non-React hosts, PowerPoint/PDF export, or editing the kit itself. It also does not redirect to alternatives.\n ✓ Fixed: review_skills_skill-quality (1) - skills/presentation/SKILL.md:1 No explicit output format is specified for the skill's primary outputs: the final completion report and the per-talk file layout. It does not say what to read first (the sample's step modules, existing registry entry style, existing CSS naming, import style) or to match them.\n ✓ Fixed: review_skills_skill-quality (1) - skills/presentation/SKILL.md:64 The verify section lists many criteria in a single dense paragraph with no numbered sequence or explicit fix-and-rerun loop. This is hard to follow and weakens the feedback loop.\n ✓ Fixed: review_skills_skill-quality (1) - skills/presentation/references/workflow.md:1 The reference duplicates SKILL.md content (anchors, monorepo rules, confirmation-before-write, gather rules, completion checks), so it is no longer a single source of truth. A single shared groupKey is the right shape for this one evolving scene. It spawns `node node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js preview` directly through process.execPath, so the child is the Vite preview server itself, not an npm or npx wrapper. stopPreview sends SIGTERM to that child, awaits its &#39;exit&#39; event (capped at 3s), then sends SIGKILL if it is still alive. Every script starts the preview and the browser inside a try whose finally runs `await browser?.close(); await stopPreview(preview?.child)`. Success, a failing check, a chromium() launch failure and any later error therefore all close the server. Repository verify returns early on build or sample failure before any preview starts. installSignalCleanup covers SIGINT and SIGTERM. Judge C fails this on two points, and neither decides the requirement. (1) The readiness-timeout branch in startPreview sends SIGTERM without awaiting. That path runs before the preview has started, so it is not one of the named post-start exit paths. It still signals the Vite server itself, not a wrapper. In inspect-presentation.mjs, the user-configurable --settle delay runs after waitForStep, and the guidance lists longer fixed settle delays as validator noise. Every script calls it in a `finally` after closing the browser: verify&#39;s render try/catch/finally, the template verify&#39;s try/finally, and inspect&#39;s try/catch/finally. It spawns `node node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js preview` directly through process.execPath, so the child is the Vite preview server itself, not an npm or npx wrapper. stopPreview sends SIGTERM to that child, awaits its &#39;exit&#39; event (capped at 3s), then sends SIGKILL if it is still alive. Every script starts the preview and the browser inside a try whose finally runs `await browser?.close(); await stopPreview(preview?.child)`. Success, a failing check, a chromium() launch failure and any later error therefore all close the server. Repository verify returns early on build or sample failure before any preview starts. installSignalCleanup covers SIGINT and SIGTERM. Judge C fails this on two points, and neither decides the requirement. (1) The readiness-timeout branch in startPreview sends SIGTERM without awaiting. That path runs before the preview has started, so it is not one of the named post-start exit paths. It still signals the Vite server itself, not a wrapper. (2) The un-awaited SIGKILL escalation fires only if the server ignores SIGTERM for 3s. In that case the awaited cleanup has already been attempted and the forced kill goes to the server process itself. The requirement asks that the server, not a wrapper, be terminated and awaited on success, on browser launch failure and on post-start errors. Lines 50-55 and the finally blocks do exactly that. It spawns `node node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js preview` directly through process.execPath, so the child is the Vite preview server itself, not an npm or npx wrapper. stopPreview sends SIGTERM to that child, awaits its &#39;exit&#39; event (capped at 3s), then sends SIGKILL if it is still alive. Every script starts the preview and the browser inside a try whose finally runs `await browser?.close(); await stopPreview(preview?.child)`. Success, a failing check, a chromium() launch failure and any later error therefore all close the server. Repository verify returns early on build or sample failure before any preview starts. installSignalCleanup covers SIGINT and SIGTERM. Judge C fails this on two points, and neither decides the requirement. (1) The readiness-timeout branch in startPreview sends SIGTERM without awaiting. That path runs before the preview has started, so it is not one of the named post-start exit paths. It still signals the Vite server itself, not a wrapper. (2) The un-awaited SIGKILL escalation fires only if the server ignores SIGTERM for 3s. In that case the awaited cleanup has already been attempted and the forced kill goes to the server process itself. The requirement asks that the server, not a wrapper, be terminated and awaited on success, on browser launch failure and on post-start errors. Lines 50-55 and the finally blocks do exactly that. })"}]}]},"audit_results":[{"id":"engineering-preview-terminated-on-every-exit","classification":"confirmed","rationale":"Both copies of preview-utils.mjs start the server with spawn(process.execPath, [node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js, &#39;preview&#39;, ...]). The child process is therefore the Vite preview server itself, not an npm or npx wrapper. stopPreview sends SIGTERM to that child and waits for its &#39;exit&#39; event, capped at 3s, then sends SIGKILL if it is still alive. In all four scripts the preview starts inside a try block, and the browser launches inside the same block. Each finally block runs `await browser?.close(); await stopPreview(preview?.child)`. These four scripts are the repository verify (lines 26-73), repository inspect (lines 43-102), bootstrap verify (lines 1-38) and bootstrap inspect (lines 43-102). Success, a failing check, a chromium() launch failure and any error thrown after startPreview returns all pass through that cleanup. The bootstrap verify script runs its build and registry checks before the preview starts (lines 9-14). If readiness times out, startPreview sends SIGTERM to the Vite process without waiting for it. That happens before the preview is ready, and the signal still goes to the server itself, so no wrapper is left with a running server. Judge C fails this on two points, and neither decides the requirement. (1) The readiness-timeout branch in startPreview sends SIGTERM without awaiting. (2) The un-awaited SIGKILL escalation fires only if the server ignores SIGTERM for 3s. In that case the awaited cleanup has already been attempted and the forced kill goes to the server process itself. Accessibility snapshot showed the “made by and-scene” link to `https://github.com/and-scene/and-scene`; no default top-left brand link appeared. Active progress/ToC entries exposed `aria-current=\"step\"` and `data-active=\"true\"`. **Finding F-01:** browse mode omits the active step title."},{"line":1210,"text":"- **Keyboard, touch, direct navigation and boundaries:** Right, Space, PageDown advanced; Left and PageUp reversed. Synthetic horizontal touch events through AXI eval moved 1→2 on left swipe and 2→1 on right swipe. Progress selection moved to index 4 and showed active index 4; selecting “THE BUILD” jumped to its first step (index 5). Previous at index 0 stayed at 0; ArrowRight at index 8 stayed at 8."},{"line":1211,"text":"- **Fixed canvas and visual composition:** Canvas element uses 880×380 dimensions; AXI observed a uniform transform scale of 0.443 at 390×844.
